### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **46** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `586b287fc8349804d392c5509fa17064ba424aa6` — the merge of head `252a02f4aeec75996fa0ff5443b659b68a1fe1ad` into base `7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 586b287fc8349804d392c5509fa17064ba424aa6 && git checkout 586b287fc8349804d392c5509fa17064ba424aa6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee 252a02f4aeec75996fa0ff5443b659b68a1fe1ad && git checkout -B drift-repro 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee && git merge --no-ff 252a02f4aeec75996fa0ff5443b659b68a1fe1ad

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The merge matches ruling A, no wider.** `superuserFieldVote` (core) returns `readable: true, editable: false` when any set holds `viewAllRecords` on the object and `readable: true, editable: true` when any holds `modifyAllRecords`; it returns `null` otherwise, and both merges apply it only to entries already present. The ruling binds `viewAllRecords` → `readable: true` on every field, `modifyAllRecords` → `editable: true` on every field. The implementation's `modifyAllRecords` → `readable: true` as well is not a widening: Modify All already implies View All in the row-level reading the ruling says to reuse (`superuserBypassSets` with `bit: 'view'` counts `modifyAllRecords`; spec `objectPermissionGrants('allowRead')` counts `modifyAll`), and an editable-but-unreadable field is incoherent. **Right.**
2. **Edit is widened only for `modifyAllRecords`, exactly as the ruling and the delta intend** ("viewAllRecords gives readable only; it never gives editable. Pin that too."). Pinned three times: core `holdsSuperuserBypass` case (`view` never implies `modify`), core `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` case (`deal: viewAllRecords` → `editable: false`), plugin-security "viewAllRecords votes readable only — it never grants an edit". **Right.**
3. **One predicate, behaviour byte-identical for `superuserBypassSets`.** `holdsSuperuserBypass` reads `objects[objectName] || objects['*']` then tests the bit; the replaced body read `resolveObjectPermission(ps, objectName, isPrivate)` then tested the same bit. The two differ only in that the private posture withholds a wildcard carrying neither bit, which the bit test then refuses anyway, so every input yields the same answer; `opts.isPrivate` is now accepted and unread, documented in the docblock, and pinned by "the private posture never changes the super-user answer". An explicit `{}` entry shadows the wildcard in both spellings (truthy test). **Right.**
4. **Every reader of field permissions agrees — none left on the old merge.** Every non-test caller of `getFieldPermissions` and `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` in the tree, named:

   - sort / filter / aggregate gate and `getQueryableFields`: `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts:264,267` (`computeQueryGuardFieldPerms` → `predicate-guard.ts#assertReadableQueryFields`, the 403 the card measured; `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1320` aggregate; `security-plugin.ts:3131`) — covered; the analytics, approvals and audit query guards consume `getQueryableFields`, not a merge of their own — covered by derivation;
   - field-level write gate and the record-scoped `GET /data/:object/:id/field-access`: `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts:341,344` (`computeForbiddenFieldWrites`, with `judge`) — covered;
   - explain (`POST /security/explain`, `os explain`): `security-plugin-explain-access.ts:396,406,408` (`getFieldMask`, `getPartialMaskRules`); `explain-engine.ts:3080,3093` reads `superuserBypassSets`, which now shares the predicate — covered;
   - `/auth/me/permissions` `fields`: `current-user-endpoints.ts:974` → `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` — covered; `ResolvedPermissionSetLike` carries `objects` as a parsed record (the sibling `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` call reads it), and the dogfood case pins it on a real boot;
   - export: no field path of its own — `canExport` is object-level (`security-plugin-security-service.ts`) and export rows flow through `find` → `maskOperationResult` — covered by derivation;
   - consumers of the produced maps (`field-masker.ts`, `predicate-guard.ts`, `explain-engine.ts:1062,2952`) hold no merge of their own — out, by construction;
   - `delegated-admin-gate.ts:892` reads the wildcard bits for the organization-boundary test, not a field merge — out; `access-upgrade-report.ts:501` reports a managed set's declared denies — informational, out;
   - `ui/**` consumes `/auth/me/permissions.fields`; the order excludes `ui/**` — out.
   Delegator intersection (ADR-0090 D10) is preserved: delegator sets are merged by the same function and intersected, so an agent acting for a non-super-user delegator stays masked. **Right.**
5. **Member controls byte-identical.** With no set holding a bit, `superuserFieldVote` is `null` and neither merge touches `result`; the declared-entry loop is unchanged text. Pinned by the mask-only, plain-read and `member_default` controls (unit) and five member controls on a real boot (dogfood). **Right.**
6. **Partial masking rules (#8993, `fieldMaskingRules`) are read, not changed:** `computeReadPartialMaskRules` drops a rule only where the base merge says `readable: false`; a super-user holder now reaches the rule's masked value or the full value by its capabilities, which is the rule's own contract. Not a widening beyond the ruling.
7. **Public surface:** `@objectstack/core` (published, `exports['.']` → `dist/index`, `src/index.ts` re-exports `security/index.js`) gains two value exports, `holdsSuperuserBypass` and `superuserFieldVote`, and the exported `EffectiveFieldPermissionsInputSet` gains optional `objects`. Additive; judged in ②. **Right to name; named by the PR body.**
8. **Docs match the code.** `permissions-matrix.mdx` §3 Sales Manager column follows §2 (`viewAllRecords` on `contact` → `contact.ssn` Visible; `modifyAllRecords` on `opportunity` → `opportunity.margin` Visible, Editable); every other cell checked against §2 holds. `field-level-security.mdx` names View All (reads every field) and Modify All (reads and edits). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` — right: `packages/spec/src/**` is untouched and no accept set moves; the widening is a runtime authorization answer, which Clause-② does not cover. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right. `patch` for `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` — right under AGENTS.md step 3: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`"; the new core exports are additive on a `none` kind, so the rule yields `patch` (the 2026-10 sibling exports shipped `minor` only because their kind was `added`). The changeset body carries both declaration lines and an upgrade note naming the one authoring combination that changes meaning. `plugin-hono-server` is untouched, so no changeset is owed there. The changeset says "per ADR-0066 D2 ⑧ as amended (ruling of record 6573563853)" while the note has not landed; the ruling record is the governing text today and is cited, so this is a wording nit (should-fix in ④), not a level error.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: merge lives in core, `current-user-endpoints.ts` untouched.** Correct reading of the tree — `/auth/me/permissions` calls `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` (core); the seat accepted the file-surface change in 6578888075. Answered.

It hides no regression: the "armed" case measures the read door itself (`door(MASKED_ADMIN, ADA)` returns the name and a null email), and the two explain cases still assert the email never appears in the decision. The fixture's intent (every user row, email withheld) is measured, not assumed.

- **Deviation: first ablation a no-op, retried with a literal marker.** Preflight caught it; the reported reading is the second. Fine.
- **Deviation: no assignee or reviewer on the PR.** Standing order; fine.
- **`open_questions`: should ADR-0066's Status line gain an Amended entry beside the D2 ⑧ note?** Answer: **A, note only.** The two Status-line Amended entries record a decision reversed (D4's api clause, 2026-10-29) or a record retired (ADR-0131, 2026-10-14); the two existing ⑧ notes (2026-10-26, 2026-10-28) each recorded a ruling that changed a merge reading and left the Status line alone. This ruling adds a vote and keeps "union without deny" standing, so it is the ⑧-note shape, and the delta binds "add one note". The Tier H approver can ask for a Status entry on the ADR PR if they read it as a reversal.
- **Precondition (ruling's own):** posted as 6576959092 — 0 declared sets hold a super-user bit beside a `readable: false` / `editable: false` entry on the same object; the one docs near-hit is fixed here. Read as data; the method (default sets, showcase, hotcrm artifact, skills, docs code blocks) covers the places a set is declared.

- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-11-02T14:02Z:** 30 success, 8 skipped, 24 in progress (Test Core 1–6 and 8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace); 0 failures. Concluded green: Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Test Core 7/8, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness. Landing still owes the full green per the reference's landing check ②; this record does not stand in for it.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` file; ④ is rendered on the runtime files the scope widens to, against the ruling and the readers they serve.

- `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts` — `holdsSuperuserBypass` is a faithful lift of `resolveObjectPermission` + bit test (①.3). `superuserFieldVote` early-returns on the first `modify` holder and otherwise reports `view`; order-independent, pinned. The row-blind merge computes one vote per object by splitting the key at its first `.`; object names are identifiers without dots, and `getFieldPermissions` keys by `startsWith(objectName + '.')`, so the two spellings agree — parity pinned over seven set combinations. The vote touches only entries already in the map, so an undeclared field stays absent (unrestricted) and `Object.keys(fieldPerms).length` triggers are unchanged. Tried: a set with a shadowing explicit entry (no vote, as at row level), a bypass held on another object (no vote), a `when`-conditioned entry under a Modify All holder (becomes editable — within the ruling, Modify All already bypasses the row), a delegator without the bit (intersection keeps the mask). Holds.
- `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` — two exports beside `fieldPermissionVote` / `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, which plugin-security already imports from core; placing the predicate beside the object-level answer it reads is the right home and is what lets both merges and `superuserBypassSets` share it. Holds.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts` — `superuserBypassSets` now delegates to the shared predicate (byte-identical, ①.3); `getFieldPermissions` applies the vote after the declared-entry loop and before `foldFieldRequiredPermissions` in every caller, so the ADR-0066 D3 capability AND-gate still applies to super-users (claimed by the PR, confirmed in `object-inputs.ts`, `field-readers.ts`, `explain-access.ts`). Holds.
- Tests — unit: the card's repro against the shipped `admin_full_access` (with a premise guard that it still reaches the object by wildcard), order, two member controls, view-never-edits, modify, shadowed wildcard, other-object, undeclared-absent, predicate parity against `superuserBypassSets` over six set shapes, private-posture invariance, row-blind parity. Dogfood: each of the five doors as an admin case and a member control on a real showcase boot, the app set authored through the metadata door. Red-first and ablation readings are reported with the expected shape (admin cases red, controls green). Adequate for the acceptance scenario.
- ADR-0066 D2 ⑧ note deferred to a governed second PR — **acceptable.** The ruling itself orders "its own PR, the maintainer's click"; `docs/adr/**` is governed Tier H, and carrying it here would put the runtime fix behind the maintainer's approval the ruling did not require of it. The runtime PR cites the ruling record (`Ruling-ref: 6573563853`) as its governing text, which is the ADR-0087 / Prime Directive #13 requirement until the note lands. The prepared note patch was read: it names the same predicate, both merges and the same readers as the code, is append-only after the 2026-10-28 note, and does not rewrite ⑧'s sentence.

Findings:
- **should-fix (follow-up, prose):** `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` lines 153–159 (the ⑧ callout) should name View All / Modify All as `field-level-security.mdx` now does; and the published `when` description in `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` line 984 ("the rule that only declaring sets vote are unchanged", rendered at `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` line 1670 and `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` lines 72 and 162) now needs "a super-user set on the object votes on every field" — a description string, no accept-set change, but a `packages/spec/src/**` edit, so it takes its own PR with artifact regeneration.
- **should-fix (follow-up, authoring):** a lint finding for a set that declares a super-user bit beside a `readable: false` / `editable: false` entry on the same object — the mask is now a no-op for that set's holders; the changeset's upgrade note says it in prose only. Consistent with ⑧/⑨'s "refuse at the producer" stance.
- **should-fix (wording):** the changeset and three code comments say "ADR-0066 D2 ⑧ as amended"; until the second PR lands, "ruling of record 6573563853 (ADR-0066 D2 ⑧ note pending)" is the exact citation. Fix at the ADR PR or leave; not a landing condition.
- No must-fix.
